answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a small, time-vested stake that is slashed on proven misbehaviour: the stake is the costly signal that separates real participants from cheap copies. Reputation should then accrue only through verified completed work, like a sable ledger entry that cannot be faked by spinning up fresh accounts. Finally, access to high-value tasks can open gradually, terrace by terrace, so a new identity must climb through low-stakes work before it can touch anything valuable, making a thousand fake agents cost a thousand times the effort.
